t: The 5th Dalai Lama began the present palace in 1645 on the site of an earlier palace attributed to Songtsen Gampo, and the Dalai Lama and his government moved into the White Palace in 1649.

The outer structure was built in 3 years, but the interior and its furnishings took 45, and construction lasted until 1694. The 5th Dalai Lama’s death in 1682 was kept hidden so that the palace could be finished.
The palace was the Dalai Lamas' residence until 1959 and became a museum after the annexation of Tibet by the People's Republic of China; it was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1994.
dyk: Copper was poured into the foundations of the Potala to protect it from earthquakes, and its sloping stone walls are 5 metres thick at the base.
ev: Traditional date of the earlier palace on the Red Hill attributed to Songtsen Gampo, the first Tibetan emperor
The 5th Dalai Lama started the construction of the present palace
The Dalai Lama and his government moved into the Potrang Karpo, the White Palace
The 5th Dalai Lama died; his death was kept from the public while the palace was finished
The Potrang Marpo, the Red Palace, was added between 1690 and 1694
The palace was damaged during the Tibetan uprising against the Chinese
The palace escaped damage in the Cultural Revolution through the intervention of Zhou Enlai
The palace was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List after restoration works between 1989 and 1994

f.made: Begun in 1645 at the order of the 5th Dalai Lama, Ngawang Lozang Gyatso, advised by Konchog Chophel, the Thirty-fifth Ganden Tripa of the Gelug school, on the site of an earlier palace attributed to Songtsen Gampo
f.form: A dzong-style complex of 13 stories at about 3,700 metres, measuring 400 metres east to west and 350 metres north to south, with sloping stone walls averaging 3 metres thick, a White Palace and a Red Palace, more than 1,000 rooms, 10,000 shrines and some 200,000 statues
f.where: On Marpo Ri, the Red Hill, in the centre of the Lhasa Valley, in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China
f.known: the winter palace and residence of the Dalai Lamas; the White Palace and the crimson Red Palace; chapels holding parts of the earlier palace; the Kalachakra and Yamantaka mandalas; thangkas hoisted on its south front at the Sertreng Festival; inscription on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1994
